jobs.description: Employer: BWX Technologies, Inc. Expires: 11/05/2026 Position Overview:Our Communications team is looking for an intern who’s passionate about connecting and inspiring people. This team member will develop content and channel strategies to engage BWXT employees throughout North America. jobs.title: Packaging Development Intern at tms
jobs.description: Employer: tms Expires: 11/05/2026 ABOUT UStms unites technology, marketing, and sourcing to drive transformational change for the world’s leading brands. With more than 1,400 employees across 28 countries., we offer an impressive range of solutions – from inspiration and innovation to category management and delivery. Operating as a creative agency, a strategic consultancy, a sourcing business, and a technology provider, we engage with over 110 million customers every single day for our clients, including McDonald’s, T-Mobile, O2, Starbucks, and adidas. Most importantly, we're a place where you can achieve great things, and be recognized as the best. WHAT MATTERS THE MOSTBreakthrough, business-driving ideas come from extraordinary people with the freedom to be their most authentic selves at work. Authenticity and diversity are critical elements of our business. They can only be realized when we create access and equity for all. We foster a culture of inclusion and belonging and aspire to be ever-evolving. tms is a place where brilliant people are better together. If you want your ideas to be heard and to contribute to a culture of inclusion and authenticity, bring us your voice! Visit us at tmsw.com. WHY WE THINK YOU WILL LOVE THIS ROLE The world's most respected brands rely on tms’s packaging expertise, supply chain analytics, and promotions management know-how, to deliver a competitive advantage for their business. Joining tms means becoming part of a dynamic team, developing innovative solutions, and delivering value to our clients across 22 countries. We know our success is derived from our people, and, as such, we continuously evolve our people practices ensuring personal and professional enrichment, while fostering a work environment that is fun, collaborative, and diverse in thought. tms is seeking an intern to support the Packaging Development team for the term June to December in our headquarters located in downtown Chicago’s West Loop. This group is responsible for designing and commercializing packaging for the Quick Service and Causal Dining Restaurant Industry. Our interns participate in exciting activities to support our fast-paced business, while working both independently and as part of cross-functional team. WHAT YOU WILL BRING TO THE ORGANIZATION Support Packaging Development team members with the following: Developing/testing for new items on our customers’ menusExecuting supplier qualifications for existing packagingDeveloping/testing innovative, compostable packaging alternatives for current packagingExploring cost-savings or operational improvement opportunities through modification of existing packagingExecuting case pack optimization to improve restaurant and/or supplier efficienciesCreate and manage packaging specifications Conduct competitive assessments of food service packaging, assemble reports and present findings to teamSupport consumer Research, focus groups, sensory/kitchen testing set-up, and field testingCoordinate and evaluate 3rdparty lab testing SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE WE WOULD LIKE YOU TO HAVE Successful tms intern candidates meet the following requirements: Pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Packaging Science or relevant fieldCompleted all prerequisite classes to be eligible by start datePrefer a minimum GPA of 3.0Demonstrated time management skills through course work and extracurricular activitiesMS Office proficiency (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook)Excellent written and verbal communicationCollaborative/teamwork oriented EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYERWe are an equal opportunity employer, and we value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. RECRUITING AGENCIEStms does not accept agency resumes submitted by third-party vendors unless a valid agreement has been signed and the tms Talent Acquisition Team has granted authorization for submissions for a specified position. Please do not submit or forward resumes to our site, tms employees, or any other company location. tms is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Graphic Design Intern at Iowa Natural Heritage Foundation
jobs.description: Employer: Iowa Natural Heritage Foundation Expires: 11/05/2026 Job descriptionAre you a creative individual who enjoys the outdoors and working in a collaborative setting? If so, apply to be part of a small communications team working to help Iowa Natural Heritage Foundation (INHF) protect and restore Iowa’s land, water and wildlife.INHF design interns gain real-world experience designing professional-quality publications, logos and graphics. The design intern works across departments to create print and digital collateral, display and marketing materials, and complete special projects. Design interns gain experience working within an established brand and representing that brand to in-person and digital audiences.Work examplesThe design intern will contribute to INHF’s quarterly magazine, annual calendar, outreach materials, project mailings, event collateral, web and social media graphics among other projects. Depending on skills and interest, other marketing, video and/or photography work may be included.Skills/QualificationsThis position usually goes to graphic design majors, journalism majors specializing in visual design or students with strong design/web experience and coursework. Knowledge of Adobe Creative Suite software is required. Experience with Squarespace, WordPress or other web content building platforms. All programs and equipment (with the exception of a personal computer if working remotely) provided by INHF.We’re looking for students who are:Interested in climate solutions, the outdoors, land protection and/or stewardshipAttentive to detailCreative, with a passion for visual designEnjoy seeking out and learning about new techniques and trendsFlexible, organized and capable of working on multiple projects with varying deadlinesComfortable collaborating with a teamThis internship is open to undergraduate students who live in or are attending a college, university or technical program in Iowa. AvailabilityTiming for this internship can be flexible with school schedules. Preference will be given to applicants who can start in January of 2027, working between 10-15 hours/week, and continuing through the summer. In the summer, interns must be available to work 32 hours/week. The internship will end in August. Pay is $15/hr. Most work will be done in the INHF office, but there will be opportunities to work remotely, assist at outreach events and visit project sites in the field. Interns must provide their own transportation to and from work, if needed. INHF encourages interns to take advantage of active and mass transit options while in the Des Moines metro area (DART system, biking and carpooling).Application informationApplication deadline is November 4, 2026. Applications should include:A one-page cover letterResume5-6 samples of your work (published/professional examples are ideal, but classroom work is also accepted). Work samples can be in a PDF or Word document format or through a link(s) (for example, to an online portfolio). One letter of recommendation from a professor or professional in your major/area of interest. The letter may be included in your application or sent separately by the author. Please include reference contact information.

jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: TV News Internship at KSNW TV
jobs.description: Employer: KSNW TV Expires: 11/05/2026 KSN is looking for an upper-level college student who is ready to jump into the world of TV news. We are looking for someone who has taken journalism classes and has some writing experience. Experience with collegiate TV production is not necessary, but great if you have it! Previous experience with print-based journalism also a plus. Internship will include working with multiple team members to learn many different skills in the newsroom (including shadowing producers, reporters, photographers, editors and other newsroom team members). After an initial training process, internship will have a specific focus of photojournalism (shooting and editing video), multi-media journalism (shooting and editing video, writing stories for broadcast and digital) and/or producing newscasts (editing video, stacking newscasts, writing for broadcast and digital) based on the skills and experience of the individual intern. Some sports coverage is expected for those who shoot and edit video (focusing on high school football). Position is for 2026/27 semesters to be determined, located in Wichita, Kansas, and will remain open until filled. There is no “normal” schedule in a newsroom, so expect to work odd hours, including weekends, early mornings, or evenings. We will coordinate your class schedule with your weekly internship schedule. We have hired some of our previous rock-star interns for full-time work – this is a great way to get your foot in the door!Internship Details :Each internship is for 15-20 hours per week for approximately 15-20 weeks Will be well supervised and participate in a meaningful learning experience Upon completion of the internship, the student will be evaluated by the internship supervisor Requirements & Skills :Must be a college junior/senior with multiple journalism classes completed Expected to work 2-3 shifts per week, hours may vary A collaborative worker with a willingness to learn Previous internship experience a plus, but not required Fluency in English, bilingual Spanish a plus Collegiate experience in news writing is required; can include AP Style writing for college newspaper, script writing for broadcast, or related assignments #LI-OnsiteSCAM ALERT:Please be aware candidates may be at risk of being targeted by scammers seeking personal data or money. Recruiters with Nexstar Media Group and its local stations will only contact you through official job boards, LinkedIn, or email with Nexstar.tv domain or official station email addresses (example:@wreg.com). Be cautious of any outreach claiming to be from Nexstar or its recruiters via any other messaging platforms or personal email addresses. We will not contact you using a @gmail email address. If you are unsure about the authenticity of a job inquiry or offer, email us at corporaterecruiters@nexstar.tv.

jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Social Media Content Intern at The Spellbound Group
jobs.description: Employer: The Spellbound Group Expires: 11/05/2026 The Spellbound Group is a social media and marketing agency working with artists, legacy estates, and lifestyle brands. We run day-to-day social, write copy, build campaigns, and report on what's working for clients across music and beyond. Our roster spans contemporary artists and some of the most storied catalogs in music, including Janis Joplin Juan Gabriel, The Doors, Henry Mancini, and John Lee Hooker, plus our parent company's affiliated brands like Trixie Mattel, Hilary Duff, Huddy, Katya, Masego, Nickelback, Zedd, Luke Hemmings, Megadeth, and more. That means one week you might be cutting a tour recap and the next you're finding a fresh way to introduce a classic album to a new generation. ** Must be in Philadelphia. This position is 95% remote, but our office is in Philadelphia, and we may need you to come into the office once or twice in a while to film content or attend a meeting. We're hiring a paid Social Media Content Intern with strong video editing skills and a knack for creative planning. jobs.description: Employer: BodyStories: Teresa Fellion Dance Expires: 11/07/2026 WHO ARE WE?BodyStories: Teresa Fellion Dance is an NYC-based non-profit contemporary dance company of womxn and non-binary individuals, officially formed in 2011, and active with individual projects since 2004. We create original dance works in collaboration with composers and artists of all disciplines, and have performed across the continental United States, Cameroon, Dubai, and in Europe at venues such as Jazz at Lincoln Center, Bryant Park Fallstage, Baryshnikov Arts Center, ICA Boston, Gibney Dance Center, ENTPE Lyon, France, with the rock band Phish, and others. We work very closely with our Musical Director, John Yannelli, to make each BodyStories performance a unique sensory experience, upholding our mission to create profound emotional responses for our audiences. In addition to creating and performing innovative works, our company is committed to connecting with diverse populations through our extensive dance education programs and community engagement workshops, as well as maintaining a stable business model to sustain our work. We collectively speak nine languages and research, perform, and collaborate with artists from five continents. In addition to our in-person education and performance programming, we have launched a virtual dance education program and several online performance programs, and are continuing to develop offerings. WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?BodyStories is looking for interns for the Spring 2027! We are seeking applicants who are detail-oriented and self-motivated. Interest in the performing arts is essential. Previous arts administration experience preferred. In addition to the following areas of focus, interns will perform general operational tasks and take on other exciting projects involved in several aspects of our BodyStories Spring 2027 programming. MARKETING & MEDIA INTERNManage company social media accounts (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok)Photo/video editingWork with Artistic Director to develop and execute marketing campaigns in relation to company events and projectsWork with Company Manager and development team to design and implement fundraising campaignsNewsletter and correspondence designDesign of print and online marketing materials(Experience with Photoshop and Illustrator is preferred) SPECIAL EVENTS & DEVELOPMENT INTERNMonthly newsletter and communicationsContent developmentWork with Company Manager to plan and coordinate donor cultivation eventsResearch and apply for residencies and performance opportunitiesResearch touring locations and venuesTouring correspondence assistanceGrant application assistanceCorporate sponsorship assistanceARTS MANAGEMENT INTERNResearch rental space availabilities and book rehearsalsMonthly newsletter and communicationsAssist with scheduling for special eventsAssist with scheduling for company events and rehearsalsWork with Company Manager and Artistic Director Assist with recruiting and scheduling for dance education programAssist with correspondence with dance students, arts organizations, and artistsGeneral administrative assignmentsContent developmentIn-person, Remote, Hybrid OptionsOur internships have traditionally involved a combination of remote and in-person work. Because of the COVID-19 crisis, we shifted to an entirely remote work environment. As the COVID-19 situation evolves, we currently have remote, hybrid, and in-person options. A fully remote internship is completely possible, and remote and in-person candidates are equally encouraged to apply. Regardless of format, our internships are highly interactive and thorough; interns will receive plenty of hands-on experience in arts management, marketing, and development during working sessions, special events, mentoring, and meetings. There are also several in-person opportunities such as performances, rehearsals, workshops, and events that interns are welcome to attend, but it is not mandatory for the internship. HOW TO APPLYPlease submit our online application form, which includes a resume and cover letter submission: https://airtable.com/appAqSZ9UwdRmXZiU/pagczrQ85RU1UywrH/form. Priority deadline is October 15, 2026., and the deadline is October 21, but we will accept applications on a rolling basis. The application cycle will close when positions are filled. The internship program will run from the week of January 11 until mid-June, 2027. Upon completion of the internship program, interns will receive a stipend. We also offer course credit for students seeking it, and free attendance at classes, rehearsals, events, and performances.Upon completion of the internship program, interns will receive a stipend. jobs.description: Employer: The Toro Company Expires: 11/07/2026 The 2027 Summer Internship Program will run from May 17, 2027, through August 6, 2027. Candidates must be available to start on May 17 and participate through the duration of the program.Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future. Who Are We? The Toro Company (TTC) has delivered market-leading, innovative products and outstanding customer care for more than 100 years. With over 11,000 employees worldwide, TTC is headquartered in Bloomington, Minnesota, USA.Our company designs and manufactures turf maintenance equipment; turf irrigation systems; landscape and lighting products; snow and ice management solutions; agricultural irrigation systems; rental, specialty and underground construction equipment; and residential turf and snow equipment. We market and sell TTC products worldwide through a network of distributors, dealers, mass retailers, hardware retailers, equipment rental center and home centers—as well as online direct to end users. What Will You Do? As a Marketing Communications Intern, you will support projects that contribute to the Sitework Systems team’s strategic goals while developing experience across content marketing, digital communications, analytics, and channel enablement.You will collaborate with Marketing Communications, Product Marketing, Sales, and other partners to help coordinate and execute a variety of marketing initiatives, including:Drafting and organizing content for social media, promotional emails, product webpages, sales literature, presentations, and other marketing communications.Supporting the execution of digital and social media initiatives, including content calendars, campaign coordination, website updates, and basic performance reporting.Helping create, update, and maintain sales and channel enablement resources, such as sell sheets, battle cards, program materials, dealer communications, and marketing guides.Conducting competitive, customer, and market research to support product launches, content development, and emerging market opportunities.Analyzing marketing and program performance using available reporting tools, summarizing findings, and identifying opportunities for improvement.Coordinating inputs, timelines, reviews, and assets for marketing projects in partnership with internal teams and external vendors.Supporting photo and video shoots, trade shows, marketing events, and ongoing go-to-market initiatives.Organizing and maintaining digital marketing assets, project files, and content libraries.Other duties as assigned. What Do You Need? To be considered for this role, an individual should meet the following minimal requirements: Current undergraduate Junior or Senior pursuing a degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, Graphic Design, or a related field. ​Self-starter with a proactive approach to learning and problem-solving. ​Interest and enthusiasm for both creative and analytical aspects of marketing. ​Strong oral and written communication skills. ​Strong organizational skills and ability to support a range of tasks. ​​Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint). Familiarity with design tools (e.g., Adobe Creative Suite or Canva) a plus. ​Experience or knowledge of landscape, construction and rental industries a plus.​​ What Can We Give You? At The Toro Company, we are always working to make sure our interns know just how valued they are. In addition to a competitive pay- The Toro Company offers interns a variety of perks, including: Dress for your day – We know you're more productive when you're comfortable, which is why TTC employees are encouraged to take advantage of our casual, corporate environment. Volunteerism – The Toro Company is proud to provide interns 8 hours of paid time to volunteer in the community. Summer Hours *Based on Location* – Enjoy a flexible schedule during the summer! By working a little more during the first few days of the week, TTC employees at certain locations are able to start their weekends early and leave by noon on Friday. Competitive Pay – Competitive compensation with an anticipated hourly rate of $20–$24. Actual rates may vary based on factors such as academic standing, business function, and other relevant considerations. The Toro Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer. jobs.title: Part-Time Marketing & Community Specialist at The Wyant Group
jobs.description: Employer: The Wyant Group Expires: 11/07/2026 Position OverviewWyant Insurance & Financial Services is looking for an energetic, outgoing, professional, and highly organized Part-time Marketing & Community Specialist to help grow our presence throughout Richmond and the surrounding community.This is a great chance for local students to gain valuable business experience while in school or complete an internship requirement. This is not a traditional desk-based marketing position. The ideal candidates will enjoy getting out into the community, meeting new people, building relationships, creating marketing opportunities, and generating leads and referrals for the agency.The primary goal of this position is to build relationships that create opportunities for our agency. This person will develop relationships with local businesses, apartment communities, dealerships, real estate professionals, contractors, community organizations, and other centers of influence while also managing key digital marketing initiatives for the agency.Key ResponsibilitiesCommunity Marketing & Lead GenerationSpend time in the Richmond community building relationships and generating quote opportunities.Visit local businesses, apartment communities, car dealerships, real estate professionals, contractors, and other potential referral partners.Develop and maintain relationships with centers of influence and passive lead sources that can consistently generate referrals and opportunities.Identify new businesses, organizations, events, and community partnerships for the agency.Follow up with community contacts and work to turn relationships into measurable leads, referrals, and quote opportunities.Look for marketing opportunities during everyday interactions throughout the community.Represent Wyant Insurance & Financial Services professionally at all times.Track community marketing activity and the results generated from those efforts.Events & Community InvolvementResearch, design, plan, coordinate, and attend local events that provide opportunities to grow the agency's presence.Identify opportunities for the agency to give back to and become more involved in the local community.Coordinate with the sales team and delegate team members to attend community events and marketing activities when appropriate.Capture photos and videos at events to use for social media and future marketing content.Social Media & Content CreationManage and consistently post content across the agency's social media platforms.Create engaging Reels and short-form videos that capture the personality, culture, community involvement, and fun atmosphere of the agency.Take photos and videos while attending events and conducting community outreach.Develop content that highlights team members, community partnerships, events, customers when appropriate, and the overall agency culture.Maintain a consistent and professional brand across social media.SEO & Digital PresenceManage and improve the agency's local SEO efforts and online presence.Keep the agency microsite accurate, current, and optimized.Help manage online reviews and identify opportunities to strengthen the agency's digital reputation.Monitor digital marketing efforts to understand what is generating traffic, engagement, leads, and quote opportunities.Structured Marketing ScheduleThis position will follow a clear, defined marketing schedule designed to ensure time is being spent intentionally and consistently.The weekly schedule will include designated time for:Field & Community MarketingCOI and Referral Partner DevelopmentSocial Media & Content CreationSEO & Microsite ManagementEvent Planning & Community InvolvementCanva & Marketing Material CreationTracking, Reporting & PlanningThere will be clear expectations around how much time should be spent out in the field versus working on social media, digital marketing, outreach, follow-up, and other responsibilities.Tracking, Accountability & Sales Team MeetingsAn important part of this position will be measuring what is actually working.The Marketing & Community Outreach Specialist will track both marketing activity and marketing results, including items such as businesses visited, COIs contacted, LinkedIn outreach, events attended, leads generated, referrals received, quote opportunities created, social media activity, and other relevant results.This person will regularly provide feedback during sales team meetings and help the team understand:What marketing strategies are workingWhat isn't generating resultsWhere leads and quotes are coming fromWhich relationships are producing referralsWhich events and community activities are worth continuingWhat messaging or approaches are generating conversationsWhat needs to be changed or improvedWhere the agency should focus its marketing efforts nextWe are looking for someone who is comfortable testing new ideas, measuring the results, receiving feedback, and continuously improving the agency's marketing approach.Success will not simply be measured by activity. Visiting 20 businesses or creating five social media posts only matters if those activities ultimately help create relationships, referrals, leads, quote opportunities, community awareness, and new business.What We're Looking ForThe ideal candidate is professional, outgoing, dependable, creative, organized, flexible, and comfortable starting conversations with new people.Because much of this position takes place outside of the office, this individual must also be self-motivated and capable of managing responsibilities independently while following the agency's established marketing plan.The ideal candidate should be:Timely and dependable, with excellent follow-through.Highly organized and capable of managing multiple relationships, events, campaigns, schedules, and follow-up activities.Outgoing and personable, with the confidence to walk into a local business, introduce themselves, and start building a relationship.Professional when representing Wyant Insurance & Financial Services.Comfortable using social media, LinkedIn, Canva, and digital marketing tools.Creative and comfortable taking photos and producing short-form video/Reel content.Comfortable working from a structured schedule and being accountable for measurable results.Able to communicate what is and isn't working and recommend adjustments.A team player who can coordinate with and help organize sales team members for events and community marketing activities.Results-oriented and motivated by generating new relationships, leads, referrals, and quote opportunities.Driving & Community TravelThis position requires frequent local travel throughout Richmond. The Marketing & Community Outreach Specialist will drive company-provided commercial/marketing vehicles while visiting businesses, attending events, and conducting community outreach.The agency will provide the vehicle and cover fuel expenses associated with approved business activities. Candidates must have a valid driver's license and an acceptable driving record.What Success Looks LikeSuccess in this role isn't measured simply by how many social media posts are created, businesses are visited, or events are attended. We want someone who can turn consistent marketing activity into real relationships and measurable opportunities for the agency.The right person will help Wyant Insurance & Financial Services become even more visible and connected throughout the Richmond community while consistently generating new relationships, leads, referrals, quote opportunities, community partnerships, and increased brand awareness.If you're outgoing, creative, enjoy meeting new people, and want a role where you can get out from behind a desk and make a measurable impact in the community, we'd love to hear from you.Compensation$20-$22/hour

jobs.title: Change Academy Internship at Marketing for Change
jobs.description: Employer: Marketing for Change Expires: 11/07/2026 Spring 2027: Change Academy Internship & Fellowship (Orlando, FL & Alexandria, VA + Denver, CO is design only) DescriptionThe Change Academy at Marketing for Change offers graduate students, college seniors and others a paid semester-long experience working and learning at one of the nation’s leading behavior-change marketing agencies. In behavior-change marketing, the objective is not sales or profits; it’s influencing behaviors in a way that leads to a healthier, safer, more sustainable world. Each semester, the Change Academy accepts three to five interns with demonstrated skills or education in marketing, advertising, writing, research, and graphic design. Interns work together with experts in their field on real-life projects and also receive both skill-specific and broader training in behavioral science. Interns participate in agency events, client meetings and (if you want) off-the clock social gatherings. Interns earn $18.40 an hour or minimum wage (whichever is higher) and work 20 hours a week, with at least one day a week in our offices. The in-office experience is critical to help interns improve their skills, work with mentors and share a group experience with other interns in their cohort. Please confirm you can participate in person at your selected location. LocationOur offices are located in Orlando and just outside Washington, DC, and we very much prefer to hire people willing to locate in those areas. Additionally, we have a design hub in the Denver area. We are mostly a hybrid workforce with staff working together in-person at least one day a week because we value the fun and collaboration that allows. The program lasts between 12 and 16 weeks depending on the semester. Instruction takes place during the first 6 to 8 weeks of the internship, mixed with group projects and real work experience. The final weeks focus on work experience and give applicants an opportunity to build an impressive portfolio. Select interns may also be asked to apply as fellows, who can work up to 40 hours a week, or to join the Marketing for Change team permanently as employees. The Change Academy is the main path to entry-level employment at Marketing for Change. Several former M4C interns are now in leadership roles at M4C, including an art director, creative director, senior media planner, and strategist.Requirements Relevant experience or college classes in a related field. Preference is given to graduate students, recent graduates or college seniors with at least one prior internship in a relevant field. Other adults with the right skills but no degree may also apply. (Several have been successful in the past.)Deep curiosity in what makes people tick.An interest in using your powers for good and making the world a better place.Being a nice person. Seriously. We want the kind of person most other people love to work with. A quick note about our hiring processApplying for a job can feel a little like sending your application out into the void and hoping a real person is on the other side. At Marketing for Change, one will be. Real people on our team review every application. We may use technology to make parts of the process easier, but when it comes to getting to know you, considering what you could bring to our team and making hiring decisions, that’s us. We know there’s a real person on the other side of every application, too. Someone who gave us their time, shared a little bit of their story and decided we might be worth exploring. We don’t take that lightly. And if you’re considering us, we’re genuinely glad you’re here. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check and Form I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification. Please submit your application by November 1, 2026, to be considered for this opportunity. We look forward to learning more about you! Location & TimingJanuary 2027 - May 2027 | Orlando, FL & Alexandria, VA + Denver, CO (design only)

jobs.title: Visuals Systems and AI Design Intern at The Autoimmune Fund
jobs.description: Employer: The Autoimmune Fund Expires: 11/09/2026 About The Autoimmune FundAutoimmune and immune-mediated diseases affect millions of people, most of them women. Yet the money has gone almost entirely one way. Of the $40.0 billion in venture funding that went to the field from 2014 to 2025, 94.4% went to drug therapeutics. Prediction, diagnostics, devices, care access, monitoring and remission maintenance shared the remaining 5.6%. The Autoimmune Fund, a seed and Series A venture fund dedicated exclusively to autoimmune and immune-mediated disease, exists to back the rest.We invest across the whole spectrum of care. We lead investments everywhere except drug therapeutics, where we co-invest. Our thesis follows three scientific revolutions reshaping the field: Immune Precision, Accelerated Aging, and Female Biology.We are a small team that runs on AI. Everything we publish, from The Autoimmune Decade, our annual report launching in January 2027, to our slides, one-pagers and infographics, runs on one visual system. We want that system to be precise enough that an AI can apply it as reliably as a trained designer. What You'll DoYou will own how the fund looks, and teach an AI to hold that standard.First project: align our visual communication system. Audit our palette, typography, icons, chart styles, grids and layout rules across documents and slides. Find where they conflict, propose the rulings, and turn the result into one clear, written source of truth with components ready to use.Second project: train Claude on our design system. Set up our brand inside Claude's design tools (Claude Design) and write the instructions and reusable skills that teach it our rules. Generate slides, one-pagers and infographics, compare them against the standard, find where the AI drifts, and fix the instructions until it stops.Then: extend the system as the fund grows. Carry the system and its AI workflows into new formats, including report exhibits, social posts and web pages, so every piece we publish looks like it came from one hand. You HaveCurrent enrollment in an undergraduate program in design, visual communication, HCI, or a related fieldA portfolio that shows at least one system, such as a brand identity, type system or component library, not only single piecesReal typographic judgment: pairing, hierarchy, grids, and setting numbers so they alignDiscipline with a constrained palette, including contrast and accessibilityAdvanced Figma: components, styles and variables, not just drawingReal, hands-on AI use. You've built prompts, custom instructions, projects or workflows in tools like Claude or ChatGPT, and you can show us oneClear writing. Training an AI is mostly turning taste into precise, testable rulesAvailability to work in person in Los Angeles Nice to HaveCoursework or lab experience in immunology, biology or another life scienceData visualization experienceBasic HTML/CSS or MarkdownInterest in healthcare, biotech or venture capital What You'll GetDirect mentorship. You work side by side with the fund's Managing Partner, a clinician and former Wall Street healthcare equity analyst who covered 500+ companies over 14 years.Work that ships. What you build goes into real investor materials and our annual report, not a drawer.Builder-level AI skills. You will design, test and fix AI systems, not just prompt them.A front-row seat to venture. See how a specialist fund sources companies, weighs science and makes decisions.A portfolio piece few undergrads have. A working design system and the AI that applies it, both built by you. To ApplySend your resume, a portfolio with at least one system project, and a short note (200 words max) describing one design rule you once had to make precise enough for someone else to follow, and what went wrong the first time to bonnie@autoimmune.fund. Work Test (3 to 4 hours, unpaid)We'll send you a packet: an excerpt of our brand rules, three past pieces of ours, and two pages of raw content (Content A and Content B). Send everything back as one PDF plus your instruction file. Unfinished parts are fine if you tell us what you would do next.1. Rule the conflicts. Our rules and our past pieces do not fully agree. List every conflict you find. For each, state the rule you would adopt and why, in one sentence. Flag anything else in the packet you think is wrong.2. Design the standard. Design a one-pager from Content A in Figma or a similar tool, by hand, with no AI-generated imagery. This is the reference the AI must match.3. Teach the AI. Write one set of instructions (a skill, custom instructions or a system prompt) that gets an AI to produce Content B in the same system. The same instructions must work on both pages. No hand edits to the AI output.4. Score it. Write at least ten pass/fail checks for this system. Score your AI output against them. An honest 7 out of 10 beats an inflated 10 out of 10.5. Show the work. Share the full chat log. In 150 words or fewer, tell us where the AI failed and what that taught you about writing instructions.

Generate slides, one-pagers and infographics, compare them against the standard, find where the AI drifts, and fix the instructions until it stops.Then: build AI workflows for a small, fast team. Training an AI is mostly writing precise, testable instructionsComfort in Figma or a similar design toolObsessive attention to detail. You notice when a teal is one shade offAvailability to work in person in Los Angeles Nice to HaveCoursework or lab experience in immunology, biology or another life scienceBasic HTML/CSS or MarkdownExperience building or maintaining a brand guide or style guideInterest in healthcare, biotech or venture capital What You'll GetDirect mentorship. You work side by side with the fund's Managing Partner, a clinician and former Wall Street healthcare equity analyst who covered 500+ companies over 14 years.Work that ships. What you build goes into real investor materials and our annual report, not a drawer.Builder-level AI skills. See how a specialist fund sources companies, weighs science and makes decisions.A portfolio piece few undergrads have. Working AI systems you built and trained. Work Test (3 to 4 hours, unpaid)We'll send you a packet: an excerpt of our brand rules, two pages of raw content (Content A and Content B), and one sample AI output. jobs.title: Videographer and Photographer Internship at Leonards Lens
jobs.description: Employer: Leonards Lens Expires: 11/12/2026 Videographer and Photographer InternshipLeonard's LensAbout Leonard's LensLeonard's Lens is a Tampa-based marketing and operations consultancy working with small businesses, nonprofits, independent artists, and community organizations. Our work spans brand strategy, digital advertising, campaign execution, and community impact. We move fast, we care about quality, and we believe great content tells a story worth paying attention to.The RoleWe are looking for a creative, dependable Videographer and Photographer Intern to join our team in Tampa. This is a hands-on, on-the-ground role. You will be the person who is there when things happen: events, community projects, artist shows, client activations, and the everyday moments behind the work. You will work directly with our founder and capture the photos and video that our social media and brand teams turn into finished content.This is an in-person internship based in the Tampa Bay area, open on a rolling basis to students in film, media, communications, photography, marketing, and related programs.What You Will DoFollow our founder, Leo Mathews, to events, meetings, community projects, and everyday work moments, capturing photo and video as they happen.Shoot photo and video at Leonard's Lens events, client events, and community activations, including live music, festivals, and neighborhood projects.Capture on-the-spot interviews, audience reactions, and short story-driven clips.Anticipate which shots will tell a complete story before, during, and after an event.Do quick edits and turn around same-day or next-day clips for Stories and Reels.Organize and label raw footage and photos in shared folders so the content team can find and use them fast.Coordinate shot lists and ideas with our social media and brand design team members.Use good judgment and discretion when capturing personal and behind the scenes moments.Expect a few shoots per week, with some evenings and weekends depending on the event calendar. Quality over quantity is the standard.What We Are Looking ForA good eye for framing, light, and storytelling. Comfort shooting with a phone or your own camera. Basic editing skills in CapCut, iMovie, Lightroom, or similar tools. Someone who stays calm in fast moving, crowded, unpredictable environments and is comfortable approaching strangers for a quick interview. Reliable transportation and flexible availability for evenings and weekends. Someone who takes creative direction well and knows how to push back respectfully when they have a better idea. Experience is less important than curiosity, work ethic, and genuine interest in community and culture.A phone camera is fine to start. If you have a camera, stabilizer, or microphone, bring it.AI tools are welcome for editing and workflow efficiency. Content that looks AI generated or feels generic is not the standard we hold ourselves to.All photos and video created for Leonard's Lens belong to Leonard's Lens. With permission, you can use approved pieces in your portfolio.Location & CompensationIn person in the Tampa Bay area, with travel to events and partner sites as needed$200/month stipend for gas and free entry and meals to events. What You Will Walk Away WithA portfolio of real photo and video work from live events, community projects, and brand campaigns. Hands-on experience in event coverage, documentary style storytelling, and fast turnaround content. An understanding of how photo and video fit into a broader marketing strategy. Direct mentorship from a working marketing professional with over a decade of industry experience.To ApplySend a short note about yourself, why this role interests you, and two or three examples of photo or video you have created. They do not need to be professional. They need to be authentic.Contact: Leo Mathews | Grow@leonardslens.com | 219.201.0312

jobs.description: Employer: Sutherland Institute Expires: 11/12/2026 Founded in 1995, Sutherland Institute is an independent research and educational institution – a think tank – whose mission is to equip Americans to advance principled public policy that promotes the constitutional values of faith, family and freedom. Sutherland is a nonpartisan, nonprofit and tax-exempt organization who relies on support from individuals, corporations and foundations that resonate with our mission. Job summary: A Policy Research & TikTok Content Internship at Sutherland Institute is a 24-hour per week paid position. A key focus of this role is conducting research on relevant public policy issues under the supervision of Sutherland Institute's policy team. Translating research into engaging digital content by brainstorming, creating, and helping manage TikTok content that connects younger audiences with the Defending Ideas podcast and other upcoming Sutherland Institute resources. Responsibilities: Policy Research & Analysis Quantitative and qualitative research and data analysis in policy areas including education, elections, religious freedom, economic opportunity, and family policy. Assisting policy team members in producing written and visual content based on policy research. Assisting with events or legislative efforts as needed. Other duties as assigned. TikTok & Short-Form Video Strategy -Brainstorm TikTok content ideas that introduce younger audiences to Defending Ideas and, as appropriate, other Sutherland Institute content. -Identify relevant TikTok trends and creative formats that make content engaging for younger audiences while maintaining Sutherland Institute’s voice, standards, and accuracy. -Review TikTok performance and audience feedback to recommend improvements that increase reach, build engagement, and encourage viewers to explore full Defending Ideas episodes. Learning Opportunities: During this internship, you will gain practical experience in: -Policy research methodologies, data analysis, and synthesis across key issue areas. -Professional written and verbal communication in a think tank setting. -Non-profit communications and public policy advocacy. -Translating complex policy ideas into accessible, engaging short-form video content. Preferred Qualifications -Interest in public policy research and/or non-profit organizations. -Interest in social media strategy -Current college student or recent graduate. -Strong writing, editing and verbal communication skills. ________________________________________________________________________________________ Position start: January 2027 Hours per week: 24 Wage/salary: This is a paid internship based on experience and availability Location: Sutherland’s office is located in downtown Salt Lake City. jobs.title: Getty Post-Baccalaureate Conservation Internship at J. Paul Getty Trust
jobs.description: Employer: J. Paul Getty Trust Expires: 11/14/2026 The Getty Post-Baccalaureate Conservation Internships aim to increase the number of students from underrepresented backgrounds preparing to enroll in graduate degree programs related to museum conservation. An advanced degree is essential to a conservation career and few programs exist. Applicants often boost their credentials by completing prerequisite courses and undertaking up to thousands of hours of conservation training, usually unpaid. Graduate program administrators say these realities have limited opportunities for underrepresented groups.Launched in 2020 as a pilot program, the Getty Post-Baccalaureate Internships are the first nationwide effort to provide yearlong financial support and hands-on conservation experience to underrepresented post-baccalaureates who are preparing to apply to conservation graduate programs. EligibilityWhile these internships are intended for students from backgrounds underrepresented in the conservation field, Getty encourages eligible candidates from all backgrounds to apply for consideration. Getty is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any protected trait under the law. Candidates will have the opportunity to demonstrate their interest in museum conservation and how they might add new and underrepresented perspectives, which can include – among other things – socio-economic status, cultural background, physical or other disability, geographical origin, and/or any other life experiences.Candidates must:-Be a United States citizen or permanent resident eligible to work in the United States (permanent residents are non-citizens authorized to live and work in the United States on a permanent basis, also known as "green card" holders). Those with DACA (Deferred Action for Childhood Arrival) status valid through the internship period are also eligible.-Be committed to a career in conservation and possess a strong desire to attend graduate school to further that goal.-Be able to demonstrate previous experience in conservation. Terms of the GrantAll positions are full-time for 12 months from September 7, 2027 — August 25, 2028. Interns are placed at conservation studios and labs at the Getty Center or Getty Villa for their first six months, and then at a local Los Angeles museum or within a different Getty department for the second six months.Grant AmountThe grant amount is $45,500 for 12 months plus $1,500 towards relocation expenses to Los Angeles. The internship includes an additional $4,000 towards educational reimbursements, certificate courses in conservation, domestic conservation conference attendance, or other professional-development opportunities related to the internship. Housing is not provided. Interns are eligible to enroll in Getty's healthcare plan at a subsidized cost. Please note that grant funds may be subject to federal and state taxes and deductions.Prerequisite Course for Graduate SchoolDuring spring 2028, interns may enroll in a prerequisite course (chemistry, art history, studio art, and/or foreign language) at a local community college to help fulfill the requirements for their graduate school applications. In addition to support from their supervisors, interns will also have the support of an academic advisor Collaborating InstitutionsInternships are offered at the conservation studios and labs at the Getty Center in Los Angeles and the Getty Villa in Malibu, along with local Los Angeles museums. For the 2027-2028 internship year, placements are being offered at the following Getty departments and institutions:Getty Conservation Institute Collections Department and Los Angeles County Museum of ArtGetty Conservation Institute Science Department and The HuntingtonGetty Research Institute Conservation and Preservation Department and the Autry Museum of the American WestJ. Paul Getty Museum Antiquities Conservation Department and the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences Margaret Herrick Library

Each year DJNF arranges paid internships for approx. 80 college students across the country and provides them with advanced hands-on training, industry mentors and a robust peer and alumni network to tap into.Interns attend one-week training programs before reporting to work in paid internships at top media companies for 10 to 12 weeks. Weekly salaries start at $525. (Median salary is $675/week)Applicants can choose which internship programs they would like to be considered for:+ Audience Engagement: These internships vary by newsroom, but the mission always remains the same—to help the news find its audience. From writing SEO-friendly headlines and producing engaging content for video and social to crafting newsletters and seizing on trending topics on social media, job expectations vary. Previous internship placements include: Palm Beach Post, The Marshall Project, Oakland Voices and Houston Chronicle.+ Business Reporting: We place reporters in more than 30 newsrooms across the country covering a wide variety of topics from Wall Street to Main Street, including markets, economic trends, new businesses, emerging entrepreneurs, labor unions, real estate, climate change, agriculture and automotive industries. Previous internship placements include: The Wall Street Journal, American City Business Journals, Barron’s, Insider, Fortune, American Banker, Detroit News and Automotive News.+ Data Journalism: There are three different types of data internships we usually place interns in: 1) heavy emphasis on filing records requests and analyzing data using spreadsheets; 2) reporting and writing using government data or assisting investigative reporting projects; and 3) using coding and technical tools to build apps and interactive visuals for news stories. Previous internship placements include: Arkansas Democrat-Gazette, Detroit News, Maryland Matters and Investigative Reporting Workshop.+ Digital Media: Working as a digital media intern means many different things, depending on the newsroom. You could be working in print, social, video, audio or all of it. Interns receive across-the-board training so they can expand their skill sets using the latest technology and storytelling techniques. Previous internship placements include: Hawaii Public Radio, Kansas City Public Television, Oakland Voices and Storyful.+ Multiplatform Editing: Editors are the final check on a story before it is published. Multiplatform editing interns assess copy for accuracy, completeness, tone and style while also writing SEO-friendly headlines and designing pages on deadline. Previous internship placements include: The New York Times, Los Angeles Times, The Washington Post, Stars & Stripes and San Francisco Chronicle.The pre-internship training dates typically fall between May 17-June 12. Internships traditionally start the first or second week of June.

jobs.title: Strategic Marketing Intern at TADA Mobility (USA) LLC
jobs.description: Employer: TADA Mobility (USA) LLC Expires: 11/18/2026 About ThrooTADA Mobility (USA), operating in New York City as Throo, is a Singapore-based ride-hailing platform that has disrupted the Southeast Asian market since its launch in 2018. Unlike traditional giants like Uber or Lyft, Throo operates on a zero-commission model. Instead of taking a large percentage of every fare (often 20% or more), Throo charges drivers a small, fixed platform fee. This ensures that drivers retain more of their hard-earned income and riders enjoy more competitive, transparent pricing.Powered by MVL’s blockchain, Throo creates a "fairness-first" ecosystem. By recording ride data securely and transparently, the platform incentivizes safe driving and high service quality through a token-based rewards system. Having already captured significant market share in Singapore, Cambodia, Vietnam, Thailand, and Hong Kong, Throo is now bringing its blockchain-backed, driver-centric model to the West, with New York City serving as the cornerstone of its North American expansion.About the RoleThroo is expanding, and we are looking for a Strategic Marketing Intern to join our foundational New York City Launch Team. NYC is the most competitive and regulated ride-hailing market globally. We need a high-velocity, intellectually curious individual to help build Throo’s brand from the ground up in New York City.You will work directly with the Launch Lead to create UGC content, design a localized messaging strategy, and execute the marketing playbook that will define Throo’s success in North America.Key Responsibilities1. NYC Market Entry & Messaging StrategyHyper-Local Messaging: Craft the "Why Throo" narrative specifically for the NYC market, differentiating us from incumbents (Uber/Lyft/Revel) for both driver-partners and riders.Segmented Campaigns: Develop bespoke messaging strategies for diverse NYC segments—from Manhattan commuters to outer-borough driver communities.GTM Execution: Support the end-to-end execution of the New York Go-To-Market (GTM) strategy across digital, OOH (Out-of-Home), and grassroots channels.Content Creation: Create User-Generated Content (UGC) or other marketing materials to onboard New Yorkers2. Stakeholder Mapping & AdvocacyInfluence Mapping: Identify and map key NYC power players, including TLC (Taxi & Limousine Commission) influencers, driver unions/guilds, and local community leaders.Partnership Scoping: Identify and vet local NYC brand partners (lifestyle, fintech, or events) for co-marketing opportunities that provide immediate "street cred" and user trust.Public Perception: Assist in managing PR efforts to position Throo as the "fairer" alternative in the NYC transport ecosystem.What You’ll NeedNYC DNA: Deep familiarity with the New York City landscape, culture, and transit habits.Creativity Mindset: Positive, experimental approach to content creationStrategic Rigor: Ability to map complex stakeholder ecosystems and translate "fairness" into a compelling, high-conversion marketing hook.Communication: "First-class" written and verbal skills; ability to hold your own in a room with senior leadership and external partners.Why This Role?Zero-to-One Experience: You aren't maintaining a brand; you are building one in the world's most famous city.High Visibility: As part of a lean launch team, your work on messaging and stakeholder mapping will be seen and used by Throo’s global leadership.Impact: Direct involvement in one of the most significant milestones in Throo’s company history.

jobs.description: Employer: The New York Historical Expires: 11/19/2026 Spring 2027 Zimmermann Decorative Arts InternLocation: New York City, New York | Hybrid | Part-Time | InternshipNew York Historical is excited to continue offering an internship funded by the Marie Zimmermann Foundation, designed to provide hands-on experience for undergraduate students with a strong interest in American decorative arts and material culture.The internship is designed for undergraduate students interested in learning about the research and study of American decorative arts and material culture and experiencing the day-to-day activities of a large history museum. Zimmermann interns will participate in the hands-on examination and cataloging of collection objects, conduct detailed design, technology, and social history research for new acquisitions and artifacts earmarked for inclusion in upcoming exhibitions, compose blogs related to collection objects and their experiences working with such material, and assist curators in artifact-based presentations. Interns will also participate in the museum’s program of expanding the collection to reflect the diversity of the city and nation today, and assist curators in locating and acquiring evocative artifacts.This internship is intended to support students interested in broadening access to careers in museum collections and curatorial work. Candidates with a demonstrated commitment to exploring historical narratives, material culture, and collections stewardship in ways that reflect a range of perspectives and lived experiences are especially encouraged to apply.The intern must be enrolled in an undergraduate program, have a strong interest in American decorative arts and material culture, and must have internet access.

jobs.description: Employer: Haworth Expires: 11/20/2026 Graphic Design Intern- Washington D.C. Company OverviewAt Haworth, we're not just creating office furniture; we're shaping dynamic workspaces. As a global leader in workspace solutions, we're on a journey to redefine the future of work. Headquartered in Holland, Michigan, Haworth is a family-owned global powerhouse at the forefront of innovation and sustainable design in the workspace interiors industry. Here, you'll get hands-on with state-of-the-art resources, interact with cross-functional teams of passionate innovators, and experience a blend of global reach and family-owned feel. You'll join a cohort of around 50 other dynamic interns for a 12-week program packed with hands on learning. Throughout the summer you will dive into real projects that will give you a taste of what it's like to work in a leading business and manufacturing environment. Sharpen your skills with interactive workshops on networking, public speaking, and using AI tools in a business environment. Connect with mentors and see all areas of the office and manufacturing processes. By the end of the summer, you'll leave with real skills, an expanded professional network, and memories to last a lifetime. This is your chance to take your career to new heights! Client Engagement Studio (CES) supports field sales client pursuit opportunities through highly customized, branded collateral, including presentations, lookbooks, marketing materials, event collateral, and template development. This is an exciting opportunity for students who wish to get hands-on experience with a broad range of public relations projects and public events within a non-profit, public media environment. A successful Communications intern will have terrific attention to detail, a desire to work on multiple projects with a variety of supervisors, and an interest in public media, history, and/or non-profits. Writing and proofreading skills are very important, along with excellent organizational skills and real enthusiasm for teamwork on events.The intern will support the WETA Communications team as it develops and execute communications and events that effectively engage audiences in the D.C. area and across the national public media system. This intern will be part of the public relations team working to support for films/projects produced by WETA and distributed to national audiences, as well as those created by/focused on the local market (such as the WETA productions WETA Arts and It's Academic and WETA Classical). The intern will also develop editorial and storytelling skills working on important corporate communications publications and branding projects.By the end of the internship, interns will have a portfolio of their own projects to demonstrate public relations skills and will have worked with senior managers in promotions, events, corporate communications, and publications.Please note that this intern will not work directly with NewsHour Productions.The WETA Communications intern will be an in-office position in WETA's Arlington, Virginia office, with occasional, pre-scheduled off-site event work. Standard administrative work hours for the company are 9-5, Monday-Friday. The internship is expected to be 3-4 days a week onsite, either Monday-Thursday or Tuesday-Friday. The internship is open to candidates able to commit at least 24 hours per week, and the internship cannot exceed 32 hours per week. The Communications team understands that candidates will have a variety of academic demands, pre-committed travel, and other scheduling issues. We will discuss mutually agreeable schedules in the interview process.All applicants must submit a cover letter and a resume. Applications without a cover letter will not be reviewed. Links to short-form writing or project samples are encouraged.PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIESSupport a busy and dedicated Communications team across corporate communications projects, events, and media outreach, including:Develop editorial skill by contributing to corporate communications projects, including photo research and editing/proofreadingAssist with a building-wide environmental design and storytelling brand projectBuild and track audiences for public events to include outreach to organizations and registration/RSVPsWork with a team on advance and day-of support for event logisticsWrite and edit blurbs/articles about tv, online and classical music programs for use in media pitching, promotions, and publicationsConduct media research, build media lists, and report on media coverage using Muck Rack databaseOrganize and categorize photo and publicity assets using digital asset management systemEDUCATIONPreferred Major: Demonstrated interest in media, history, arts, theater, humanities, communications and/or public affairsLEARNING OBJECTIVESUnderstand the public media system and the many opportunities for careers in the fieldGain broad knowledge and direct experience in a range of corporate communications and media relations roles in working for a major content producer at a leading non-profitApply learned writing, editing and proofreading skills to real-life publications and situations, with your own specific projects to showcase your skillsDESIRED COMPETENCIESProactive organizationArchival/research skillsWriting and proofreadingCollaborative and flexible teamworkAttention to detailPlus, bring your special extra skills, i.e. photography, graphic design, languages, talent management, public events, etc.ADDITIONAL SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONSHelpful to have fluency in Excel, Claude, Word, PowerPoint, and other softwareLOCATIONWETA and NewsHour Productions are Washington, DC established media and news organizations. We are a largely local workforce based out of the Campbell Place office in Arlington, VA. WETA and NewsHour Productions value employee flexibility when possible. Most positions based in our Arlington, VA office will be onsite or hybrid, depending upon the role.COMPANY OVERVIEWWETA, the flagship public media station in the nation's capital, produces and distributes content that informs, inspires, and enriches lives.As the second-largest producing station for the public media system, WETA creates programming to explore history, arts, and culture, partnering with acclaimed filmmakers such as Ken Burns and Dr. Henry Louis Gates, Jr. National WETA productions include The American Revolution and Finding Your Roots, among many others. WETA is also home to PBS News, the primary daily, breaking, and special news producer for PBS. Its broadcast productions include PBS News Hour, Washington Week with The Atlantic, Horizons from PBS News, and Compass Points from PBS News, as well as specials, documentaries, and a robust footprint across digital platforms.Locally, WETA serves audiences across Washington, D.C., Virginia, and Maryland, through television, radio, and digital platforms. Audiences access WETA on broadcast channels WETA PBS, WETA UK, WETA Metro, WETA World, and WETA PBS Kids, and digitally through the free streaming platform WETA+. Listeners tune into WETA Classical, the exclusive home for classical music in the Greater Washington area, via radio, online, and the WETA Classical app.EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITYWETA and NewsHour Productions are equal opportunity employers committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.This policy applies to all employment practices within our organization, including hiring, recruiting, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, leave of absence, compensation, benefits, training, and internships. Through our unique mentorship program, we empower future leaders to step into the world of entrepreneurship, gain invaluable business experience, and build a foundation for long-term success. As we enter our 41st year, our mission remains stronger than ever: to inspire and develop the next generation of innovators, helping them achieve extraordinary outcomes in their careers and communities. Our part-time Business & Operations Internship is designed for students looking to gain real-world experience throughout the Fall–Spring semester. Interns will support business setup, recruitment, and day-to-day administrative operations while gaining exposure to the behind-the-scenes work that helps drive a successful organization. This is a Part-time, on-site internship in Shelby Township MI running from November through end of April/ Early May 2026, with a pay rate of $14.75-$15.00 per hour. As we celebrate 41 years of empowering students and building leaders, we are proud of our mission, culture, and the positive impact we have made. If you are ready to grow your skills while making a direct impact on our business, we would love to have you on our team. Take the first step toward your entrepreneurial future, apply today!

jobs.title: Marketing Intern — Social Media & TikTok Content at Vitablabla
jobs.description: Employer: Vitablabla Expires: 11/21/2026 Job title: Marketing Intern — Social Media & TikTok Content Job type: Internship (part-time) Work setting: Remote (U.S. only) Compensation: $20/hour + 5% commission on sales generated by your videos — 1099 independent contractor. The role begins with a paid working interview: 8 videos × $30 ($240 total stipend with free sample). Hours: ~10–25 hrs/week, flexible around class schedules About UsOHCRISP is a growing U.S. snack brand making seriously crunchy freeze-dried fruit snacks. We're looking for a marketing intern who wants real, hands-on social media experience — not coffee runs and shadowing calls. You'll create TikTok content for a real consumer brand, see exactly how your videos perform, and learn how creator-led commerce (TikTok Shop) works from the inside. Our interview process — two steps, no busywork Step 1: A 30-minute video chat. A quick hello — we get a feel for your personality and on-camera presence, and you can ask us anything. No trick questions, no case studies. Step 2: A paid working trial. Film 8 videos for us over ~2 weeks and get paid $30 for each video you submit ($240 total, paid after each submission via Venmo/Zelle). You show us what you can do, we pay you for it — and if it's a fit, you continue as our marketing intern. Free product provided, obviously. What you'll do as an intern Create TikTok videos featuring OHCRISP: taste tests, snack reviews, trending formats, dorm-life content, ASMR crunch videos Brainstorm hooks, formats, and content series with our team Track what's working and help shape our content strategy. Who this is for Currently enrolled U.S. college student, 18+ Native English speaker, comfortable appearing on camera and speaking in videos You already make TikToks — or have always wanted an excuse to start Interested in marketing, social media, content, or consumer brands as a career pathNo followers, no formal experience required Happy to complete paperwork if your school offers internship credit Submitted videos must meet a basic content checklist (shared upfront). By submitting content, you grant OHCRISP the right to use approved videos on our brand channels, website, and paid ads How to applyUpload your resume and link 2–3 videos you've made (personal TikToks/Instagram are fine). We review applications on a rolling basis.

jobs.title: MBA Marketing Intern at Graco Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Graco Inc. Expires: 11/21/2026 The purpose of this position is to provide immersive, strategic-level experience within Graco’s Category Marketing team. At Graco, Category Marketing focuses on understanding and growing specific customer segments and industries (often referred to as market verticals), helping the business identify opportunities, understand customer needs, and shape strategies that drive growth. In this role, the intern will lead a defined strategic project for an assigned customer segment under the mentorship of the Director of Category Marketing. The intern will leverage market research, Voice of Customer (VOC) insights, competitive analysis, and go-to-market strategy to address a real business challenge. The experience culminates in the development and presentation of a strategic recommendation to Graco’s Executive Leadership Team. This internship is designed for MBA candidates seeking a long-term career in category marketing, product marketing, strategic marketing, or general management. Program Structure: This summer internship is centered on a high-value strategic project that addresses a real business opportunity or challenge within an assigned category and which has the potential to shape future growth initiatives. The project is supplemented by exposure to the broader category marketing function and close collaboration with cross-functional partners, including product management, channel marketing, corporate marketing, and sales. The internship culminates in a strategic recommendation presented to senior internship. What You Will Do at Graco Strategic Project Experience Lead a high-impact strategic project focused on a real business opportunity or challenge within an assigned customer segment or industry. Work closely with a Category Marketing leader to define the project scope, conduct analysis, and develop recommendations. Apply market research, customer insights, and business strategy concepts to address a meaningful business question. Develop and present a final recommendation to senior leaders at the conclusion of the internship. Market and Customer Insights Conduct market, customer, and competitive research to better understand industry trends and customer needs. Analyze Voice of Customer (VOC) feedback and other data sources to identify key insights and opportunities. Learn how customer and market insights are used to shape busness and marketing strategies. Cross-Functional Collaboration Collaborate with teams across product management, sales, channel marketing, and corporate marketing Gain exposure to how strategy is developed and translated into product launches, marketing campaigns, and commercial execution. Coordinate with internal subject matter experts to validate research findings and assumptions. Participate in team meetings, project reviews, and business discussions to better understand Graco's growth strategy. Professional Development Build skills in strategic thinking, business analysis, executive communication, and problem solving. Receive coaching and mentorship from experienced marketing leaders throughout the internship. Develop and deliver a professional executive-level presentation summarizing project findings and recommendations. Other duties and learning opportunities as assigned. What You Will Bring to Graco Currently pursuing an MBA, with an expected graduation date within 12–18 months of the internship Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business Administration, or a related field Prior experience in marketing, business strategy, or vertical-specific market development (internship or professional) preferred Team collaborator with experience working in multi-functional or global team settings Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret and synthesize VOC insights and market research into clear recommendations Excellent communication and presentation skills, including comfort presenting to senior leadership Ability to manage ambiguity and drive a project forward with limited day-to-day direction
